concepts.title: Understanding Acids, Bases and Their Chemical Properties
concepts.definition: Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red, bases are bitter and turn red litmus blue; acids react with metals to give hydrogen gas, with metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to give carbon dioxide, and acids neutralise bases to form salt and water.
concepts.key_idea: Acid plus base gives salt and water; acid plus carbonate bubbles carbon dioxide.

concepts.title: pH Scale - Strength and Importance
concepts.definition: The pH scale from 0 to 14 measures how acidic or basic a solution is: pH 7 is neutral, below 7 acidic, above 7 basic; plants, soils, our mouth and digestive system all work within careful pH ranges, so pH knowledge guides farming, health and even antacid use.
concepts.key_idea: Seven is the balance point: below is acid country, above is base country.

concepts.title: Salts and Their Families
concepts.definition: Neutralisation produces salts, whose solutions may be neutral, acidic or basic depending on their origin: sodium chloride is neutral, washing soda is basic, baking soda is mildly basic, and bleaching powder, plaster of Paris andPOP-family salts find wide daily use.
concepts.key_idea: Salts inherit character: strong-acid-strong-base pairs stay neutral, others lean acid or base.
